draft.title: The electromagnetic spectrum
card: Visible light is one part of a family of waves called the electromagnetic spectrum. All of these waves carry energy and can travel through a vacuum.
In order from longest wavelength to shortest, the family is radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays.

Moving along the spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays, the wavelength gets shorter and the frequency gets higher. Higher-frequency waves carry more energy. Ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays have the most energy, and this decides both their uses and their risks.

Each band has common uses. Radio waves are used for broadcasting. Microwaves are used for cooking and mobile phones. Infrared is used for remote controls and heaters. Ultraviolet is used for sterilising. X-rays are used for imaging bones. Gamma rays are used for treating cancer.
draft.remember: Light is one kind of electromagnetic wave. The kinds differ in wavelength, frequency and energy. High energy decides the uses and the risks of ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays.

a.q: Which statement about visible light is correct?
opts: It is one of several kinds of electromagnetic wave
It is the only kind of wave that can cross a vacuum
It has the shortest wavelength in the spectrum
It moves faster than radio waves through a vacuum
a.why: Visible light sits in a family with radio waves, X-rays and others. All of them can cross a vacuum and all travel at the same speed there, so light is not special in either way. Gamma rays, not visible light, have the shortest wavelength.
a.clue: Think about which waves are in the same family as light.

b.q: The Sun sends other electromagnetic waves to Earth as well as visible light. Which comparison with visible light is correct?
opts: Ultraviolet has a shorter wavelength than visible light
Ultraviolet has a longer wavelength than visible light
Infrared has a higher frequency than visible light
Infrared moves faster than visible light through space
b.why: Ultraviolet lies past violet in the spectrum, so its wavelength is shorter than visible light's. Infrared lies on the other side, with a longer wavelength and a lower frequency, and all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum.
b.clue: Recall the order of the spectrum and which way wavelength changes along it.
